incidents-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING: High error rate observed in serving-pool-east (multiple CUDA OOMs). Paging on-call @sara (oncall). Link: <https://redwood.internal/incidents/2425000001>

sara (oncall): I'm on it. grabbing coro logs and nvidia-smi from the affected node now.

devin (eng-runtime): seeing repeated `cudaErrorOutOfMemory` from the runtime even though allocator reports headroom. attaching snippets.

devin (eng-runtime): `kubectl -n serving logs pod/runner-7f8c -c runtime --since=15m`
```
[2026-02-28T01:23:12Z] ERR cudaMalloc failed: out of memory (attempting 2684354560 bytes)
[2026-02-28T01:23:12Z] WARN reserve_pool_free=2 reserve_pool_reserved=5 reserve_chunk=134217728
[2026-02-28T01:23:12Z] INFO kv_cache_attempt_alloc=2600000000 contiguous_required=true
```

devin (eng-runtime): `nvidia-smi topo --matrix && nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.free,memory.total --format=csv`
```
GPU 0: 6144 MiB free, 16384 MiB total
GPU 1: 5632 MiB free, 16384 MiB total
```

devin (eng-runtime): so OS-visible free memory ~6GB but the runtime fails allocating contiguous ~2.5GB.

raj (infra): possible fragmentation or reserved blocks fragmenting addressable space. can you dump allocator state (we have a debug endpoint)?

devin (eng-runtime): hitting debug endpoint now: `GET /internal/allocator/state`
```
allocator_version: v3.2.1
free_regions: 124
largest_free_region: 790000000  # ~0.79GB
reserved_blocks: 5
reserved_block_sizes: [268435456, 134217728, 134217728, 268435456, 67108864]
largest_contiguous_free: 790000000
```

devin (eng-runtime): allocator has many small free blocks; largest contiguous is ~0.79GB which explains failure for 2.6GB contiguous alloc.

sara (oncall): customer impact? maria, any alerts from support?

maria (customer-ops): seeing errors from 3 Dedicated customers and a few Hosted routes. error rate peaked ~6% for affected routes, started 01:22 and spike lasted ~14 minutes. we've opened tickets for impacted accounts and posted a short status.

sara (oncall): OK. triage plan: (1) remove serving node from rotation (cordon/drain), (2) restart runtime container to free fragmented reserves, (3) enable fallback routing to quantized-variant for high-latency traffic, (4) follow-up postmortem + telemetry.

raj (infra): cordoning node gpu-node-13 now.

raj (infra): `kubectl cordon gpu-node-13` -> success. doing `kubectl drain` with `--ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data`.

infra-bot: drain job started for gpu-node-13, draining 7 pods. ETA ~30s.

devin (eng-runtime): restarting runtime on the last pod instead of cold-evicting entire node to keep capacity. restarting runner-7f8c.

devin (eng-runtime): restart accomplished. after restart we see process mem map resets and allocator reports: `largest_contiguous_free=14800000000` (-> ~14.8GB), requests succeed.

sara (oncall): good — are we sure restart prevented immediate recurrence or is this a transient fix?

devin (eng-runtime): restart fixed symptom but root cause is allocator fragmentation + reserved-block sizing that prevents merging small free blocks into a large contiguous region. the reserve policy pre-allocates many mid-size chunks that now block a large contiguous allocation.

raj (infra): enabling fallback routing at the edge router: `routerctl set-fallback serving-pool-east --model redwood-small-q4` -> applied.

infra-bot: router config change pushed to 3 gateways. :white_check_mark:

maria (customer-ops): posting update to impacted customers: short blip, most traffic retried successfully after 2nd attempt; affecting synchronous generation calls. error rates back to baseline for Hosted; 2 Dedicated tenants saw degraded throughput during drain window.

sara (oncall): handing off primary to raj for infra-led mitigation and long-term fixes. I'm staying as incident lead for comms and postmortem. @raj please track.

raj (infra): taking over. immediate mitigations implemented. longer-term fixes being proposed:
- surfacing `largest_contiguous_free` and `reserved_block_count` to console and alerts
- change default reserve_chunk size to better align with common KV cache allocation patterns
- implement coalescing path to merge adjacent free blocks on deallocation
- add an emergency soft-evict that frees KV cache first before failing user allocations

devin (eng-runtime): creating follow-up ticket INC-3421 with proposed fixes and a repro harness. attaching a small repro that allocs many mid-sized reservations then requests a large contiguous alloc.

maria (customer-ops): support follow-up: we've offered 1:1 sync with impacted enterprise customers and a credit where appropriate. tracking in CRM.

sara (oncall): timeline:
- 01:22 UTC: first OOMs reported by telemetry
- 01:24 UTC: paging alerted oncall
- 01:28 UTC: node cordoned/drain + runtime restart
- 01:36 UTC: fallback routing enabled
- 01:44 UTC: error rate returned to baseline

sara (oncall): incident status: mitigated. leaving open for postmortem. last update at timestamp 2425000520.

raj (infra): note: we'll also add a dashboard panel showing fragmentation (free_regions, largest_contiguous_free) and an alert when largest_free < 2*x p99 alloc size. filing frontend/dashboard ticket.

devin (eng-runtime): quick note for the postmortem: include allocator debug endpoints, nvidia-smi snapshots, and per-pod reserve metadata. recommend adding per-request metadata to attribute failures to reserve fragmentation when present.

sara (oncall): thanks all. tagging `@eng-runtime @infra @customer-ops` for follow-ups. :v:

pagerduty-bot: Incident 2425000001 acknowledged by sara (oncall). Priority: P2.

incidents-bot: Incident mitigated — follow-up actions recorded in INC-3421. Postmortem owner: devin (eng-runtime).
